kp_title: Determining Whether a Set of Functions is Orthogonal With Respect to a Given Inner Product
raw_html:
1.Determining Whether a Set of Functions is Orthogonal With Respect to a Given Inner Product?

Consider the following set of functions: f1(t)=cos⁡t,f2(t)=sin⁡(2t),f3(t)=t

Given that the inner product in the vector space C[0,π] of continuous functions over [0,π] is defined as ⟨f(t),g(t)⟩=∫0πf(t)g(t)dt, which of the following statements are true?

  1. f1(t)⊥f2(t) with respect to the given inner product
  2. f1(t)⊥f3(t) with respect to the given inner product
  3. S={f1(t),f2(t),f3(t)} is an orthogonal set with respect to the given inner product
